Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the p95/p99 qualification path (hosted Redwood API vs your incumbent):

Key asks/targets from the call:
- Primary KPIs: end-to-end p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 480ms (for your interactive search workload).
- Throughput envelope to validate: 100–140 req/s steady-state with short bursts to 220 req/s for 60s.
- Streaming behaviour: chunked responses with avg 3 chunks per response; concurrency: up to 6 concurrent streams per user pod during peak.
- Sequence length: typically 512 tokens; worst-case test at 1024 tokens.

What Redwood will do:
- Run a 72-hour shadow test against hosted API (no traffic diverted) using your anonymized traffic replay.
- Collect tail latency (p95/p99), end-to-end (client->Redwood->client), per-chunk latency for streaming, and token-level throughput.
- Provide a report with latency envelope, concurrency scaling curve, and suggestions (batching, cache warmups, quantization profiles).

What we need from Orbital to proceed:
1) A 48-hour sample of production traffic (anonymized): request/response timestamps, request sizes, streaming chunk sizes. Prefer S3 link or the attached zip.
2) A confirmation of the target test window (we proposed May 4–6 UTC window).
3) Any rate-limiting or IP allowlist entries for the Redwood test agents.

Attached: redwood-shadow-test-plan-v1.pdf (contains the harness, metrics collection spec, and data handling notes).

Next steps / timeline summary:
- You provide traffic sample + allowlist by EOD Tue (Apr 30).
- Redwood schedules shadow run (3 days) and sends preliminary results within 48h of completion.

If the targets above look off from your side, flag the numbers and we’ll adjust.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up if helpful.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes

Thanks — read the plan and sample traces quickly. High-level checklist and proposed configuration for the shadow run: 

1) Harness / probes
- Traffic replay: preserve original inter-arrival times for the steady-state window; add two burst scenarios (60s @ 220 rps, 30s @ 320 rps) to exercise buffering.
- Instrumentation: collect client-side send timestamp, Redwood receive-ts, Redwood send-ts, client receive-ts. This lets us compute network + processing + serialization split.
- Streaming: capture per-chunk emit timestamp and chunk size; compute per-chunk latency and total response latency.

2) Measurement methodology for p95/p99
- Compute end-to-end p95/p99 on per-request complete latency (client send -> client receive). For streaming, both total response latency and per-chunk p95/p99 will be reported.
- Exclude requests with client-side backpressure (identified by >200ms pre-send queuing in the sample).

3) Warm vs cold start
- Warm run: pre-warm KV cache using 2x baseline traffic for 30m prior to measurement window.
- Cold run: clear KV and run a 1-hour cold window immediately after to capture worst-case.

4) Concurrency and sequence lengths
- Concurrency matrix: run test sets at 2, 4, 6, and 8 concurrent streams per user pod.
- Seq lengths: 512 (primary), 1024 (stress).

5) Expected outputs and thresholds (for initial pass)
- Hosted goal: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 480ms (as Camila noted).
- If we observe p99 > 620ms then escalate and run profiling with kernel-level traces.

6) Ops notes
- Need OAuth token allowlist and S3 access details from Orbital.
- We'll post results to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-shadow-tests and create a short dashboard (Datadog link TBD).

Proposed schedule (UTC times):
- May 04 00:00 — pre-warm (30m)
- May 04 00:30 — warm measurement window (24h steady-state + burst scenarios applied)
- May 05 00:30 — cold-start measurement window (1h)

If that works we’ll lock and I’ll kick off the agents. Ben/Laura — please confirm the customer comms and allowlist instructions.

-Jonas
